title: Special Act on Strengthening Competitiveness of and Providing Support for the Petrochemical Industry
title_original: 석유화학산업의 경쟁력 강화 및 지원에 관한 특별법
full_text:
SPECIAL ACT ON STRENGTHENING COMPETITIVENESS OF AND PROVIDING SUPPORT FOR THE PETROCHEMICAL INDUSTRY

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to contribute to responding to the climate crisis and developing the national economy by establishing a foundation for sustainable growth, including the structural advancement of the petrochemical industry, and strengthening the competitiveness of the petrochemical industry.

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act are defined as follows:
1. "Petrochemical industry" means an industry prescribed by Presidential Decree that is related to the production of basic petrochemical feedstocks from petroleum, natural gas, biomass, etc., or the production of products such as synthetic resins, raw materials for synthetic fibers, and synthetic rubber using those feedstocks as principal raw materials.
2. "Core strategic petrochemical technology" means technology prescribed by Presidential Decree that is necessary for the transition of the petrochemical industry toward high added value and for reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
3. "Transition toward high added value" means business innovation activities meeting the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree, including the production of high-value-added products with high scarcity, profitability, environmental performance, etc., and increasing added value through cost innovation.
4. "Petrochemical business operator" means a person who engages in the petrochemical industry.
5. "Business reorganization" means business reorganization under Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the Special Act on the Promotion of Corporate Vitality.
6. "Business reorganization plan" means a business reorganization plan under Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Special Act on the Promotion of Corporate Vitality.
7. "Enterprise with an approved business reorganization plan" means a petrochemical business operator whose business reorganization plan has been approved under Article 10 of the Special Act on the Promotion of Corporate Vitality.

Article 3 (Responsibilities of the State, local governments, etc.)
① The State and local governments shall formulate and implement comprehensive policies to promote the development of the petrochemical industry.
② The State and local governments shall provide administrative and financial support necessary for the policies under paragraph ① and endeavor to establish an institutional foundation for the development of the petrochemical industry.
③ Petrochemical business operators shall cooperate with the policies of the State and local governments for the structural advancement of the petrochemical industry and endeavor to contribute to strengthening the competitiveness and development of the petrochemical industry.

Article 4 (Relationship with other Acts)
This Act shall prevail over other Acts with respect to special provisions on support for, and regulation of, the petrochemical industry: Provided, That where the application of another Act is more favorable to a petrochemical business operator, that Act shall apply.

CHAPTER II SUPPORT FOR STRENGTHENING COMPETITIVENESS OF THE PETROCHEMICAL INDUSTRY

Article 5 (Tax support)
To strengthen the competitiveness of the petrochemical industry, the State and local governments may provide tax support, including tax reductions or exemptions, or apply special provisions concerning the treatment of deductible expenses, asset revaluation, tax deferral, etc., for business reorganization and transition toward high added value by petrochemical business operators, as prescribed by relevant tax statutes, including the Restriction of Special Taxation Act and the Restriction of Special Local Taxation Act.

Article 6 (Financial support, etc.)
To strengthen the competitiveness of the petrochemical industry, the State and local governments may provide fiscal and financial support necessary for business reorganization and transition toward high added value.

Article 7 (Promotion of regulatory special provisions, etc.)
① To promote business reorganization and transition toward high added value by petrochemical business operators, the Government may undertake the following measures as prescribed by Presidential Decree:
1. Integration or simplification of procedures for authorization and permission, etc. in the fields of environment, firefighting, construction, energy, and safety in connection with the development of industrial complexes, construction or expansion of production facilities, improvement of production processes, closure of facilities, etc.;
2. Special regulatory provisions concerning unavoidable exceedance of environmental standards arising in the course of industrial structural transition;
3. Expedited measures addressing insufficient technical verification or evaluation standards necessary for applying new technologies or shifting to new processes.
② The head of a central administrative agency intending to undertake any measure specified in paragraph ① shall consult in advance with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies.

Article 8 (Special provisions concerning reporting of business combinations)
① Where an enterprise applying for business reorganization under Article 9 of the Special Act on the Promotion of Corporate Vitality, or an enterprise with an approved business reorganization plan, requests an examination under Article 11 (9) of the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act at least 60 days before the date of reporting a business combination in accordance with a business reorganization plan (including a business reorganization plan approved on or after January 1, 2025; hereinafter the same shall apply in Article 9), the Fair Trade Commission shall complete its examination within 30 days from the date of the report and notify the enterprise of the results: Provided, That where the Fair Trade Commission deems it necessary, it may extend the period by up to 60 days notwithstanding the proviso to Article 11 (7) of the same Act.
② Matters necessary for the examination period of business combinations under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree after consultation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies.

Article 9 (Special provisions concerning concerted acts)
① Where an enterprise with an approved business reorganization plan jointly engages with another petrochemical business operator in any of the following acts pursuant to the business reorganization plan and obtains approval from the Minister of Trade and Industry under paragraph ②, authorization under Article 40 (2) of the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act shall be deemed granted:
1. Consultation on adjusting facility operating rates, reducing production volume, or curtailing output;
2. Consultation necessary to stabilize supply and demand, including adjustment of production volume by item and shipment schedules;
3. Joint production and investment to reduce supply capacity or rationalize processes, and joint use of related infrastructure;
4. Joint purchasing of energy, raw materials, etc. for manufacturing products;
5. Joint research and technology development.
② Where an act falling under any subparagraph of paragraph ① satisfies all of the following requirements, the Minister of Trade and Industry may approve the act with the consent of the Fair Trade Commission:
1. The petrochemical industry is experiencing an industrial crisis, such as structural oversupply, deterioration of profitability, or decline in international competitiveness;
2. The circumstances under subparagraph 1 cannot be overcome through the independent business rationalization efforts of petrochemical business operators;
3. The concerted act is limited to the minimum necessary scope for stabilizing supply chains, promoting technological innovation, responding to environmental changes, etc. in the petrochemical industry and is expected to have a substantial effect on industrial restructuring or increasing efficiency;
4. The act does not involve unfair discrimination among participating petrochemical business operators or unduly restrict their participation in or withdrawal from the concerted act.
③ Where at least two enterprises with approved business reorganization plans (including enterprises intending to apply for approval of a business reorganization plan) notify the Fair Trade Commission, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, of the following information and exchange such information only to the minimum extent necessary for business reorganization of the petrochemical industry, Article 40 (1) 9 and paragraph (5) of the same Article of the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act shall not apply:
1. Information essential to considering business reorganization, including facility operating rates, production capacity, unit consumption (meaning an indicator of the consumption of resources such as energy and raw materials per unit of production), and profit or loss by product;
2. Non-public management information shared during due diligence and review for mergers or integration of facilities.
④ Detailed criteria, procedures, and other necessary matters for applying special provisions under paragraphs ① through ③, including the scope and methods of information exchanges for business reorganization, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree after consultation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies.

Article 10 (Special provisions concerning integrated energy supply)
Article 9 (2) 4 of the Integrated Energy Supply Act shall not apply to a person intending to supply integrated energy (limited to heat supply) to an enterprise with an approved business reorganization plan during the business reorganization period.

Article 11 (Support for research and development)
① To promote research and development of core strategic petrochemical technologies, the Government may undertake the following projects as prescribed by Presidential Decree:
1. Priority support for national research and development projects and reductions or exemptions of technology royalties;
2. Installation of shared infrastructure, such as pilot facilities and evaluation facilities, and establishment of systems for their utilization;
3. Introduction of public certification and evaluation systems and support for market access to facilitate the early commercialization of products incorporating core strategic petrochemical technologies;
4. Support for research and development projects based on public-private cooperation jointly involving industry, academia, government-funded research institutes, etc.;
5. Support for international standardization of high-value-added, carbon-neutral, and environmentally friendly technologies.
② The Government shall prepare measures to improve accounting standards or ease financial burdens in connection with policy financing so that expenses for research and development of core strategic petrochemical technologies are not excessively recorded as liabilities in the accounts of private enterprises.

Article 12 (Support for personnel training)
The Government may support matters necessary for training specialized personnel and providing education and training to incumbent employees to facilitate technological development, changes in production structures, and sustainable growth in the petrochemical industry.

CHAPTER III SUPPORT FOR EMPLOYMENT AND LOCAL ECONOMIES

Article 13 (Employment support)
① The Government may provide support necessary to relieve employment instability and protect workers that may arise when petrochemical business operators undertake business reorganization or rationalize facilities to address excessive production capacity.
② The Government may provide administrative and financial support for employment to a petrochemical business operator whose workforce temporarily decreases due to business reorganization, considering its potential for growth, plans for expanding employment, etc.
③ Matters necessary for support under paragraphs ① and ② shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 14 (Support for local economies)
The Government may provide necessary support to minimize adverse impacts on local economies, including decreases in employment and damage to subcontractors caused by business reorganization, etc. in areas where petrochemical business operators are located.

CHAPTER IV ESTABLISHMENT OF FOUNDATION FOR STRENGTHENING COMPETITIVENESS OF THE PETROCHEMICAL INDUSTRY

Article 15 (Compilation of statistics concerning the petrochemical industry)
① The Government shall compile and manage statistics concerning the petrochemical industry to establish a foundation for strengthening its competitiveness and to systematically formulate support policies.
② The Statistics Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the compilation of statistics under paragraph ①.
③ The Government may have a relevant specialized institution compile and manage statistics under paragraph ① as prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, it may subsidize all or part of the expenses incurred in performing the duties within budgetary limits.
④ Other matters necessary for compiling and managing statistics under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 16 (Surveys of import trends, etc.)
① To respond to changes in petrochemical markets and stabilize supply and demand, the Government may survey and analyze trends in imports of petrochemical products, including import volumes and prices, and provide the results to relevant enterprises, etc.
② The Government may have a relevant specialized institution perform surveys and analyses under paragraph ① as prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, it may subsidize all or part of the expenses incurred in performing such duties within budgetary limits.

CHAPTER V SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 17 (Submission of data and inspections, etc.)
① Where necessary for supervision, the Minister of Trade and Industry or the head of a relevant administrative agency may require institutions, corporations, organizations, etc. related to the petrochemical industry to report on their affairs or submit data. Institutions, corporations, organizations, etc. receiving such a request shall comply unless doing so is unavoidable.
② The Minister of Trade and Industry or the head of a relevant administrative agency may have public officials under his or her jurisdiction enter offices, places of business, or other premises of institutions, corporations, or organizations related to the petrochemical industry referred to in paragraph ①, inspect relevant documents, question relevant persons, or take other necessary measures.
③ A public official who enters premises and conducts inspections under paragraph ② shall carry identification indicating his or her authority and present it to the persons concerned.

Article 18 (Delegation and entrustment of authority or duties)
① The Minister of Trade and Industry may delegate part of the authority under this Act to Mayors/Do Governors or heads of Sis/Guns/Gus (meaning the heads of autonomous Gus) as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
② The Minister of Trade and Industry may entrust part of the duties under this Act to specialized institutions, corporations, or organizations related to the petrochemical industry as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDA <Act No. 21251, 2025.12.30>

Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Act shall enter into force on the date prescribed by Presidential Decree within six months after the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Effective period)
Articles 8 and 9 shall remain effective until December 31, 2028: Provided, That the effective period may be extended by up to three years following a review of the necessity for extension upon its expiration.

Article 3 (Applicability)
Articles 5, 8, and 9 shall also apply to acts performed by petrochemical business operators on or after January 1, 2025.
